hints: Notice both starting materials are tertiary halogenoalkanes reacting with aqueous NaOH, so think about what type of substitution occurs and what the organic product will be.
Start with the yield calculation by finding moles of 2-bromo-2-methylbutane used, $30.18 / 150.9 = 0.20$ mol, so the same moles of alcohol should form in theory.
To compare rates, recall that the slow step breaks the C-X bond, so consider which bond, C-Br or C-Cl, is weaker and breaks more easily.
walkthrough:
**Identify product X**

Both are tertiary halogenoalkanes with aqueous NaOH, so hydrolysis by nucleophilic substitution gives the alcohol. Product X is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$.

$$M_r(\text{X}) = (5 \times 12.0) + (12 \times 1.0) + 16.0 = 88.0$$

**Find theoretical yield**

Moles of bromoalkane used set the maximum moles of product, as the ratio is 1:1.

$$\text{moles used} = \frac{30.18}{150.9} = 0.20 \text{ mol}$$
$$\text{theoretical mass of X} = 0.20 \times 88.0 = 17.6 \text{ g}$$

**Calculate percentage yield**

Compare the actual mass obtained to the theoretical maximum.

$$\text{percentage yield} = \frac{12.32}{17.6} \times 100 = 70\%$$

**Compare relative rates**

Both are tertiary, so reaction is $S_N1$. The rate-determining step is formation of the carbocation by breaking the C-X bond. The C-Br bond is weaker and longer than C-Cl, so it breaks with lower activation energy. Therefore reaction 1 (bromo) is faster than reaction 2 (chloro).

options.A: Rate part is correct (1 faster than 2) but yield is wrong. 41% comes from forgetting to calculate the correct $M_r$ of the alcohol product (88.0) and using a wrong theoretical mass. The correct yield is 70%.
options.B: Both parts are wrong. Yield is 70%, not 41%, and reaction 1 is faster, not reaction 2. Choosing this suggests confusing bond strength, thinking C-Cl breaks more easily than C-Br.
options.C: Correct on both counts. Percentage yield is $(12.32 / 17.6) \times 100 = 70\%$ and reaction 1 is faster because the weaker C-Br bond breaks more readily in the $S_N1$ rate-determining step than C-Cl.
options.D: Yield part is correct (70%) but rate is reversed. Reaction 2 is not faster. C-Cl is stronger than C-Br, so the chloroalkane forms the carbocation more slowly. This traps students who think chlorine being more electronegative means faster leaving.
